title: The silver instrument: Lambda transplants — field-generic rule, object-specific selectivity
claim_one_line: THE SILVER INSTRUMENT (5 agents, both adversarial lenses HOLD, the build re-derived 41/41 before use): SU(4)_2 built exactly — 10 primaries, kappa = 6, Sigma.Sigma-dagger = 864 I = 4*6^3 (the silver instance of the golden 75 = 3*5^2), S in Q(zeta_24), T forcing Q(zeta_48), the weld splitting 7 even / 3 odd exactly R,L-invariantly; the group |<R,L>| = 18432 = 2^11 * 3^2 with TRIVIAL scalars, 252 classes, purely {2,3}-primary (no order-5 — kappa = 6 has no room for a 5) and NOT a direct product (a proper Goursat subdirect, kernels 2 and 8, common quotient 1152) against the golden's clean 2T x 2I; THE TRANSPLANT (AC3): the odd sector is 3-dimensional (CP^2, as the design warned to check), projective image 384, FIVE exceptional orbits (3/24/24/64/128/192) plus 27 reflection-fixed lines, and Lambda run VERBATIM returns the full minimal orbit — size 3, stabilizer 128, all three points RATIONAL so the Galois criterion passes automatically — AC3's verdict: THE RULE IS FIELD-GENERIC (a template), ITS SELECTIVITY OBJECT-SPECIFIC (golden: 2-of-12 by the sqrt5-flip, real Galois work; silver: rational minimal orbit, trivial criterion; the discriminator is where the stage's irrationalities live relative to the odd sector); L149's cascade half: the machinery transplants verbatim, B684/G2's k = 1 row reproduces with a sharper mechanism (odd block forced to dimension 1), but the k = 2 banked value does NOT — the quadruple-derived fresh value is delta = 1 + sqrt2 (B684's own k = 6 value; their k = 2 says 1/delta), a six-variant convention sweep ruling out artifacts: B684's ladder carries a k-indexing/inversion defect, addendum-beside owed and written, the deeper golden theorems typed genuinely-open on silver.
